decision.hypothesis: The recorded floor–payload penetration is the proximate state-qualification defect that prevented the native capability calculation from proceeding; paired local diagnostics of the same incomplete execution should reproduce that prerequisite failure without revealing an independent solver or finite-state defect.
decision.expected_observation: Both diagnostic repetitions identify the recorded floor–payload contact or associated contact-free state-support failure as the first qualification blocker and recover no separate finite-state, constraint-support, or solver-entry defect.
decision.weakening_observation: Either repetition reaches the same rejection while contact-free with finite supported state, or identifies an additional independent numerical, constraint-support, or solver-progress failure that would remain after removing the recorded contact.
decision.fixed_conditions: Use the exact saved candidate and incomplete native execution, frozen central_high reach task, standardized zero-state initialization, six tendon channels with 0–8 N bounds, 0.02 s control period, 0.6 s horizon, and the recorded native model assumptions. Do not alter design, task, controls, initial state, model, or acceptance criteria.
decision.stopping_condition: Stop after the two prescribed diagnostic repetitions, or earlier if the diagnostic formally identifies an independent qualification blocker; do not infer task feasibility, infeasibility, or acceptance from this diagnostic.
decision.interpretation: This action distinguishes a contact-associated prerequisite rejection from a broader state-validity or numerical failure within the recorded execution. Reproduction would support only the contact-blocker mechanism for this attempt; it would not establish that removing contact makes the task feasible. A contact-free repeat with the same failure, or discovery of another blocker, would redirect the next investigation toward state support or solver progress rather than geometry alone.
